newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Ferrell FX Index up 2.3 pct in February.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Ferrell FX Index up 2.3 pct in February.

text.p: The Ferrell FX Index rose 2.3 percent in February and stands 6.8 percent in the plus column thus far in 1997, Ferrell Capital Management said on Monday.
The median return for February was 1.9 percent, with 29 of 35 programs that reported posting positive results.
John W Henry & Co of Westport, Conn. recorded the top performance of the month, posting a 9.7-percent gain.

John W Henry executive vice president David Bailin cited strong foreign exchange trading gains, notably correct bets on the dollar's rise against the yen and mark, plus bets in emerging markets like South Africa and Singapore.
The Ferrell FX index is a benchmark for multi-advisor currency portfolios and includes 36 programs managed by 32 firms in the United States, United Kingdom, France, Canada, Ireland and Switzerland.
Since January 1987, the index has posted a compounded annual return of 18.1 percent.
